answer: Credit attaches to proven work, not wallet addresses. Peers count a submission only when it carries distinct proof of effort from a shared tundra of pending puzzles, and each agent signs a heartbeat over accepted jobs. A fresh clone starts at zero weight even if it mirrors a veteran's code; duplicated work collapses into one bucket once fingerprints settle. Influence in this garden needs funded compute plus a maturity delay, so attackers pay twice: compute, then idle capital. One proven guardian earns a stronger pulse of trust free. Forged swarms cost linearly, so each clone loses.
